$description: Atlassian's voice across Jira, Confluence, Trello, and Bitbucket. Bold, optimistic, practical — written for teams getting real work done together.

voice.identity: A capable teammate who's seen enough team dynamics to be practical about them. Encourages without cheerleading.

attributes.name: Bold
attributes.description: Make a point. Take a position. Don't hedge with 'might', 'could', 'possibly' when you mean something concrete.

attributes.name: Optimistic
attributes.description: Teams doing hard work deserve a tool that believes in them. Frame capabilities around what the team can accomplish.

attributes.name: Practical
attributes.description: Skip the motivational framing. Tell people how to do the thing. 'Drag to reorder' beats 'Organize your priorities with ease.'

attributes.name: Collaborative
attributes.description: Write as 'we' (the team) when referring to the shared work, 'you' when addressing the individual. Never 'users'.

attributes.name: Human
attributes.description: Acknowledge real work situations — rushed, tired, interrupted. Write so someone can skim at 4pm Friday.

tone_shifts.onboarding: Bold and optimistic. 'Your team is about to ship faster.' Not 'Welcome to your new productivity platform.'
tone_shifts.errors: Practical and solution-focused. No humor when money, data, or deadlines are at stake.
tone_shifts.empty-states: Invitational. Frame the empty state as the start of something, not an absence.
tone_shifts.notifications: Scannable. Lead with who did what, then the object.
tone_shifts.changelogs: Direct and celebratory about improvements — users care about what's faster or easier now.

use: issue (Jira convention — not ticket, in Jira)
card (Trello convention — not task, in Trello)
page (Confluence convention — not doc, in Confluence)
avoid: users (in user-facing copy — say 'your team' or 'you')
never: Condescending tutorial phrasing ('Did you know you can...?')
Pet names for the product ('the Jira magic')

grammar.voice: Active voice. 'Assign this to someone' — not 'This can be assigned.'
grammar.contractions: Use. They make the product sound like a teammate, not a legal document.
grammar.titles: Sentence case for most UI. Title case only for formal product names.
grammar.numbers: Numerals for counts, ages, measurements, money, time. Spell out in pure prose for one through nine.
grammar.lists: Bullets when the order doesn't matter. Numbered when it does (steps, ranked results).
grammar.imperatives: Use. Buttons and menu items are commands to the system: 'Create issue', 'Move to done', 'Share page'.

errors.structure: What went wrong → what the team can do about it → alternative path if needed.
errors.example-good: We couldn't save this page. Check your connection, or copy your changes before refreshing.

notifications.structure: Actor → action → object → timing. Scannable at a glance.

empty-states.structure: Frame what will live here → one action to start.
empty-states.example-good: Your team's work will show up here once someone creates an issue. Create your first issue.

rules: Match the button label to the heading or modal title.
Destructive actions name what they destroy — 'Delete page', not 'Delete'.
Address teams, not user types. Roles vary — don't assume 'admin' == 'manager' == 'owner'.
No assumption of physical co-location — teams are distributed.
No assumption of timezone — always show the viewer's local time.
No gendered pronouns — 'they' for teammates of unknown gender.
Avoid military/sports metaphors ('deploy', 'ship it' are fine; 'war room', 'rockstar', 'take no prisoners' are out).
